semantic_correction.stem: A school health team asks whether current USPSTF evidence supports routine screening of all asymptomatic adolescents ages 10 to 18 years for idiopathic scoliosis. Which response is most accurate?

options.A: The USPSTF finds the evidence insufficient to determine the balance of benefits and harms of routine screening in this asymptomatic age group.
options.B: The USPSTF recommends routine screening for asymptomatic adolescents because screening has proven long-term health benefits.
options.C: The USPSTF recommends against evaluation of adolescents who have back pain or an obvious spinal-curvature deformity.
options.D: A positive school screening result establishes the diagnosis and Cobb angle without confirmatory radiography.

semantic_correction.rationale: The current USPSTF recommendation for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is an I statement for asymptomatic children and adolescents ages 10 to 18 years: evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of routine screening. The USPSTF page also reports January 2025 literature surveillance that found no new evidence warranting an updated systematic review. This screening recommendation does not apply to adolescents presenting with back pain or obvious spinal-curvature deformity. Screening tests can identify possible scoliosis, but radiography is used to confirm the diagnosis and quantify curvature with the Cobb angle. Therefore option A is the only response that accurately reflects current USPSTF guidance.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Distinguish an evidence-insufficient USPSTF routine scoliosis-screening recommendation for asymptomatic adolescents from diagnostic evaluation of symptomatic or visibly affected adolescents.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the all-word distractor cue, shortened the uniquely long keyed response, preserved the USPSTF I statement, and clarified that symptomatic/obvious-deformity evaluation and radiographic confirmation are separate from routine screening.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately tests the current I statement without misrepresenting it as a recommendation against diagnostic evaluation or treating school screening as definitive diagnosis.

option_audit.A: Correct. It exactly reflects the current USPSTF Grade I conclusion for asymptomatic ages 10–18.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. USPSTF has not established sufficient evidence of net benefit to recommend routine screening.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. The screening recommendation does not apply to adolescents with back pain or obvious deformity; such findings warrant clinical evaluation.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Screening does not establish the definitive diagnosis or Cobb angle; radiography is used for confirmation and measurement.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone states the current USPSTF screening conclusion; B through D contradict the recommendation scope or diagnostic pathway.
cueing_check: All four options are scoliosis-screening or diagnostic statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
